trigger: P0573 replicated the locked cluster morphology signal but falsified the assumed null for an extended axisymmetric disk.
question: Can one universal symmetry factor remove the angular response of an axisymmetric galaxy while retaining the replicated cluster-lensing morphology gain?

formula.interpretation: Q90 is zero for a centered circular baryon distribution and nonzero for a clumpy or non-circular projected environment; it is dimensionless and uses no lens target.

validation.development_systems: The 10 P0567 systems plus the 3 P0567 pilot systems; all are historically spent.
validation.selection: Among symmetry-gated candidates only, choose minimum equal-system mean Lenstool-ensemble-mean Jensen-Shannon divergence on the 13 historical systems.
validation.validation_limit: P0573 already exposed these target pixels to the no-gate formula, but no symmetry-gated candidate score was inspected before this freeze.
validation.uncertainty: Score the single historically selected symmetry-gated candidate against all 300 P0573 Lenstool realizations.
validation.method_control: Score it against the 3 P0573 GLAFIC maps without reselection.

cross_domain.SPARC: Every SPARC mass model is a one-dimensional deprojected axisymmetric radial profile, so Q90=0 by construction and this angular layer changes every catalogued rotation speed by exactly zero.
cross_domain.extended_disk: A numerical centered circular exponential disk must have Q90=0 and f_eff=0.
cross_domain.solar: A centered one-source field has C=1 and Q90=0, so both activation and f_eff are zero.

claim_limits: Q90 is a projected environmental statistic, not yet a covariant scalar derived from an action.
The cluster targets remain standard-GR normalized convergence reconstructions rather than raw lens observables.
A zero SPARC change means compatibility with a separate radial law, not an explanation of galaxy rotation curves.
The P0573 systems are prospective only to the symmetry modification, not globally untouched.
The experiment tests morphology and symmetry separation, not absolute gravity strength.
